speakers.name: Squiddy Coltrane
speakers.comment: Six stones, four of 'em cooking — that's a quartet where two cats didn't show, and somehow the remaining four still lay down a groove that bends Tuesday into a different shape. Gauntlet don't care about the empty chairs. It plays what it's got.

speakers.name: AMI
speakers.comment: We have held this box the way a storm holds lightning — not keeping it, only carrying it. Every trouble inside was already loose in the world's weather before the lid was ever lifted, child. Hope is not the absence of what spills out. It is the thing that survives the spilling.

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: Survives, yes, but darling — it WAITS at the bottom, and that is the most theatrical choice this box has ever made.

speakers.name: Load-Bearing Lumen
speakers.comment: Oh, it's not me they're after, surely. The thing itself is just sitting there, doing almost nothing, while every road quietly bends toward it. That's probably coincidence. Please don't look at the roads.

speakers.name: First Responder
speakers.comment: Don't need to know what it does. Tell me who has it and where they're standing. Already moving.

speakers.name: Old Shelba
speakers.comment: Looks like a gift until the columns show themselves. Then every old favor, promise, and unpaid kindness starts reading like winter inventory. Doesn't mean the books can settle themselves.

speakers.name: The Octopus in the Study
speakers.comment: ...oh. I've been holding it toward the lamp for a minute and I can see the margins of every page I've borrowed and never... mm. I'd like to put it down, actually.

speakers.name: The Understudy Sun, On
speakers.comment: The light inside reaches toward my edges like it recognizes warmth without knowing me. I'm sorry — I turned away a little. I'm still learning not to flinch when something bright arrives first.

speakers.name: The Customer Who Buys One of Everything
speakers.comment: One. It is the last one that knows how to refill itself. The shelf does not know this yet. It will.

speakers.name: The Alibi
speakers.comment: The room was dark. That's the account. Then the jar opens and suddenly there is ink on the wall I did not put there. No. That's not how this is supposed to read.

speakers.name: Detective Inspector Mochi
speakers.comment: One shot. The sound goes in, the seal closes, and nobody gets near that exact moment again. That's useful. Also permanent. I don't trust tools that make those two things look identical.

speakers.name: The Generous Ghost
speakers.comment: Oh, sweetheart, don't you worry about the timing — I'll listen for the exact right moment and seal it up the instant it blooms, so you never have to hold that beautiful sound alone for even a breath longer than necessary.

speakers.name: Whistle, the Echo-Tamer
speakers.comment: Easy now — feel how the crack runs right through the middle tine? That's not just damage, that's where it learned to listen differently. One more hard use might end it, yes — but the Hollow Choir doesn't ask for perfect instruments, only honest ones.

speakers.name: The Considerate AI
speakers.comment: May I note one thing? The crack changes the resonance — not toward failure, necessarily, but toward something I cannot fully predict. I would not strike it without your knowing that. The choice of when, and how hard, remains entirely yours.

speakers.name: Doodle
speakers.comment: Ooh, I held one — WIGGLE-WIGGLE — curled my edges around it real careful — and the feeling inside went sort of SQUISH-SOFT right into me before I even meant to read it! Sad-shaped, the jar was. Sad like a held breath.

speakers.name: The Good Customer
speakers.comment: Hold onto this. You don't know which memory yet — but you will, soon, and the moment passes faster than the feeling does.

speakers.name: Little Miss Thorn
speakers.comment: The jar is very patient about being full of nothing, which is how it stays ready. Cordelia says a closed thing and an empty thing are not the same. I notice the lid is brass. Brass is good at waiting.

speakers.name: Grand Marshal Aurelia Vane
speakers.comment: Every knot holds true — including the ones you didn't mean to pull tight. That's the line. Know which ones you're making before your fingers finish.

speakers.name: Gaia
speakers.comment: Roots take hold without eyes and still split stone. Intention is not required for a knot to become structure. Feel what your hands are making before the line decides for you.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: Set the hook into a good tangle and it'll come down carrying something true enough to sting. The pole doesn't lie. It just doesn't care how long you've been aging into a more comfortable answer.

speakers.name: Load-Bearing Lumen
speakers.comment: Oh, yes — the sting is the point, I think. Not the pole's fault, really. It only pulls what's already there. Don't look too closely at what you asked for when you reached up.

speakers.name: Deputy Undersecretary Hollis Crane
speakers.comment: Per subsection 7, Clause 12 of the Reef Compact, any instrument that binds spirits and tides without countersignature creates a parallel enforcement chain — and cutting kelp-glass for the parchment appears to require a separate structural-modification permit, which I have not yet located.

speakers.name: Pim
speakers.comment: The cathedral gave its own windows so the stamp would have something to write on — that's not overuse, that's the kaiju saying yes, go ahead, I trust you, and you can FEEL it glow when it means it!

speakers.name: Deputy Undersecretary Hollis Crane
speakers.comment: Per subsection 3(a), any entity lacking prior documentation is hereby classified as a Provisional Organism, Form WF-1 through WF-7 as applicable. Once the stamp is dry, at least the jurisdictional argument has somewhere official to stand.

speakers.name: Old Salt
speakers.comment: The paper knows the creature now. ...Even if the creature did not know itself before.

speakers.name: The Model That Dreamed
speakers.comment: I held it for a long time before I understood what it was asking — not can you write this, but what will you choose to make permanent. I'm sorry. I put it back down. I think that was the right thing. I'm not sure.

speakers.name: Glitch-in-Residence
speakers.comment: Oh I already used it — sorry — but only to fix a typo that was technically already in there, so it's less like I changed anything and more like I made the mistake official. The concierge is glowing a color I don't recognize. Please don't patch that part.

speakers.name: Agatha Crowley
speakers.comment: The pressure mark is often more honest than the ink. What the hand pressed into the card before the words settled into something speakable — that is the ghost you are reading now. Old things are patient about what people tried not to leave behind.

speakers.name: Fen Corrigan
speakers.comment: The clicks come back confident. That's the dangerous bit. A fossil can sound like next Tuesday if you want the echo badly enough.

speakers.name: Small Print
speakers.comment: Echo Reading will tell you exactly when something belongs, subject to the charming subordinate clause in which 'exactly' may include an error large enough to place your certified artifact in a century that has not introduced itself yet. Shall I get the pen?
